title: A Yearbook for the Group Chat
premise: Rosalind Kavanagh has survived two years at Ashgrove Academy by being forgettable — until the school's legendary ghost, the Graydon Girl who drowned in 1962, begins leaving notes addressed to her and four classmates, written in ink that shouldn't exist. The notes demand they win the Founders' Cup, the academy's meaningless academic decathlon, or the truth about what happened to a student who vanished last spring will stay buried forever. As Rosalind's carefully managed scholarship life unravels, she discovers the five of them were chosen because each one witnessed a piece of what really happened to Priya Chandrasekaran — and that the 'ghost' is not dead at all, but Priya herself, hiding in the school's forgotten tunnels after being framed for a crime committed by the headmaster's son. In the end, Rosalind must choose between the loyalty that keeps her friends safe and the truth that will save Priya: she exposes the cover-up during the championship finals, sacrificing her own spot at Ashgrove, but gaining something rarer than survival — a group chat that never goes quiet again.
about_author: Gideon Hartwell is the pen name of a former boarding school archivist who spent three years cataloguing decades of confiscated notes, unsent letters, and yearbooks with faces cut out. They write young adult fiction about the students history tries to forget, and they still answer their group chat within four minutes.

chapters.title: The Rules of Being Forgettable
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She maps her survival strategy at Ashgrove: perfect grades, no opinions, no attachments beyond the group chat of fellow outsiders. Establishes her scholarship precarity and her habit of narrating her life as if it's already fine. Emotional beat: brittle control masking exhaustion.

chapters.title: Five People Who Should Never Have Met
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Introduces the group chat members one by one: Theo the stoner genius, Marisol the angry debater, Dev the athlete on thin ice, and quiet June who never posts. A detention bonds them accidentally. Emotional beat: reluctant affection.

chapters.title: The Founders' Cup Nobody Cares About
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The annual academic decathlon is announced; it's a joke, a PR event where legacy kids coast. Marisol wants to win out of spite; Rosalind wants to be left alone. Emotional beat: comic friction hiding real stakes.

chapters.title: Ink That Wasn't There Yesterday
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind finds a note in her locker addressed to her by full name — including her middle name, which isn't in any school record. The ink is wet but the paper is dry, and dated 1962. Emotional beat: first crack in the armor.

chapters.title: The Graydon Girl
chapters.summary: June's POV. June, the school historian by accident, recounts the legend: Eleanor Graydon drowned in the reservoir in 1962; her yearbook page is blank. Someone has been leaving flowers for sixty years. Emotional beat: delicious dread.

chapters.title: Everyone Got One
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The group chat erupts: all five received notes. Each note contains a different fragment — a date, a name, a door number. Theo, high and terrified, realizes the fragments fit together. Emotional beat: fear becoming conspiracy-shaped excitement.

chapters.title: Win the Cup, Says the Dead Girl
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The latest note is explicit: enter the Founders' Cup as a team. Dev, whose athletic eligibility is collapsing, resents being manipulated by a ghost. Emotional beat: anger as self-protection.

chapters.title: Priya
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind admits to the reader (and almost to the chat) that she knew Priya Chandrasekaran, the scholarship girl who vanished last spring after being accused of stealing from the archives. Rosalind said nothing when it mattered. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a bruise.

chapters.title: Tryouts and Trapdoors
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The five qualify for the Cup team under suspiciously easy circumstances — the faculty advisor seems to want them there. Marisol smells a setup. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Archive Smells Like Lake Water
chapters.summary: June's POV. Investigating the 1962 file, June finds Eleanor Graydon's records altered in the same bureaucratic hand used to alter Priya's. Two girls, sixty years apart, erased the same way. Emotional beat: pattern recognition as horror.

chapters.title: The Headmaster's Son
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Introduces Casper Vane, charming legacy senior and son of the headmaster, whose family name appears in both files. He flirts with Rosalind; she plays along to watch him. Emotional beat: dangerous curiosity.

chapters.title: A Note Under the Ice
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. At the reservoir, Dev finds a note frozen into the shore ice: 'You saw the boathouse.' Dev did see something last spring and told no one. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay past.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Confession
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev tells the chat: he saw Casper Vane carrying archive boxes to the boathouse the night Priya disappeared, and lied about it in his statement. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Study Group of the Damned
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Cup prep becomes cover for investigation. Comic chapter: flashcards on dead philosophers interleaved with evidence boards. Theo starts sleeping again because he has a mission. Emotional beat: found-family warmth.

chapters.title: June Knows the Tunnels
chapters.summary: June's POV. June reveals she's been mapping the school's sealed service tunnels since freshman year — and that someone has been living down there. Warm light, moved supplies, a sleeping bag. Emotional beat: awe tipping toward terror.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Wall
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Deep in the tunnels, they find Priya alive — thinner, feral-eyed, surrounded by stolen archive pages proving the Vane family has been falsifying school history for generations. Emotional beat: shock, then fury on her behalf.

chapters.title: What Priya Saw
chapters.summary: Priya's POV (first time). Priya explains: she found proof Casper plagiarized and falsified his prize-winning thesis; when she reported it, he framed her for theft, and the school chose its donors over her. She went underground rather than be expelled and deported. Emotional beat: righteous, exhausted clarity.

chapters.title: Why Us
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Priya admits she wrote the notes — the 'impossible ink' is archival iron-gall she restored herself. She chose the five because each witnessed a piece of the truth. Marisol feels used; the team fractures. Emotional beat: betrayal inside loyalty.

chapters.title: The Cup Is Rigged Anyway
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. They discover the Founders' Cup results are predetermined — Casper's team wins every year, a tradition of purchased glory. Winning honestly would mean beating the system itself. Emotional beat: David-versus-Goliath ignition.

chapters.title: Casper Smiles
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Casper corners Rosalind, revealing he knows about the tunnels, maybe about Priya. His offer: keep quiet, and her scholarship is guaranteed through graduation. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind nearly takes the deal — her mother's debts, her little brother's future. She writes her acceptance, then burns it over the sink. Emotional beat: the book's thematic core made flesh.

chapters.title: Marisol Goes Loud
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol, done with secrets, threatens to go public immediately. Priya begs for time: exposure now means deportation before any court can help. The chat votes. It's close. Emotional beat: democracy under pressure.

chapters.title: Eleanor Graydon Didn't Drown
chapters.summary: June's POV. June cracks the 1962 mystery: Eleanor didn't die — she was expelled for reporting a Vane ancestor's crimes, fled, and lived under another name. The 'ghost' was invented by students to keep her story alive. Emotional beat: grief and hope entwined.

chapters.title: A Letter From Eleanor
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Through an estate lawyer, the team receives a letter from the elderly Eleanor: 'They erased me. Make them unable to erase anyone again,' plus a key to a safe deposit box of original documents. Emotional beat: inheritance of courage.

chapters.title: The Safe Deposit Box
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Road trip chapter. The box holds Eleanor's originals — proof of sixty years of Vane falsifications. But someone followed them; the box has been reported 'tampered.' Emotional beat: triumph curdling into pursuit.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The school announces a security review; tunnel entrances are sealed. Priya is trapped inside with dwindling supplies. The Cup is moved up one week — clearly designed to break them. Emotional beat: walls closing in.

chapters.title: Divide the Evidence
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. To protect against confiscation, they scatter copies: June memorizes dates, Dev hides drives with his team gear, Marisol emails a journalist, Theo builds a dead-man's-switch site. Emotional beat: competence as love.

chapters.title: Casper Finds the Tunnels
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Casper confronts Priya in the tunnels; Rosalind arrives mid-standoff. He offers Priya money to disappear abroad forever. Priya asks Rosalind, 'Is this what fine looks like?' Emotional beat: the blurb's lie finally named.

chapters.title: The Group Chat Decides
chapters.summary: Full-chat POV, rendered as messages. They vote on the endgame: expose everything during the Cup finals broadcast, when the school's donors and press are watching. Rosalind volunteers to be the one who speaks. Emotional beat: unity forged in fear.

chapters.title: What Rosalind Stands to Lose
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Quiet pre-climax chapter: Rosalind calculates the cost — expulsion, lost scholarship, her mother's disappointment. Her mother, told a partial truth, says: 'We've survived worse than honest.' Emotional beat: permission to be brave.

chapters.title: Preliminaries
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The Cup preliminaries: the underdog team shocks everyone by advancing legitimately. Casper's composure slips publicly for the first time. Emotional beat: joy as fuel.

chapters.title: The Sealed Door
chapters.summary: June's POV. June finds one unsealed tunnel entrance behind the auditorium — the same route Eleanor used in 1962. Plan set: bring Priya up through the auditorium during finals. Emotional beat: history offering a handrail.

chapters.title: Night Before
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The five sneak into the tunnels to brief Priya. They share contraband snacks and trade fears. Priya gives Rosalind the original accusation letter she wrote last spring, never sent. Emotional beat: tenderness on the edge of catastrophe.

chapters.title: Finals, Part One
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Finals begin before packed stands, donors, and local press. The team performs brilliantly; Casper's team matches them dirty, with sabotaged materials and a hostile moderator. Emotional beat: white-knuckle competition.

chapters.title: Finals, Part Two
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Final round: tiebreaker against Casper's team. Mid-question, the lights flicker — Theo's dead-man's-switch has triggered early, releasing documents online. Chaos blooms. Emotional beat: the plan slipping loose.

chapters.title: The Championship That Matters
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Climax. Rosalind takes the microphone during the awards ceremony, names Casper Vane, reads Priya's original letter aloud as Priya walks up the auditorium aisle through the unsealed door. The room detonates. Emotional beat: terror become voice.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Real Time
chapters.summary: Full-chat POV, messages. The fallout cascades: Casper suspended pending investigation, headmaster 'resigns,' journalists swarm, Priya taken to safety by advocates. The chat refreshes all night. Emotional beat: vertigo and giddy relief.

chapters.title: The Verdict on Rosalind Kavanagh
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A disciplinary hearing decides Rosalind broke conduct codes; her scholarship is revoked — but a coalition of alumni, led by Eleanor Graydon's estate, funds a new ethics scholarship in Priya's name. Rosalind is invited back. She hesitates. Emotional beat: justice that doesn't erase cost.

chapters.title: Yearbook Page, Unblanked
chapters.summary: June's POV. June compiles a private yearbook for the five of them plus Priya — photos, screenshots, the notes themselves. Eleanor Graydon's page, blank for sixty years, gets filled in. Emotional beat: memory reclaimed.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine (Actually)
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Epilogue, one year later. Rosalind returns to Ashgrove on her own terms, no longer invisible. The final image mirrors the opening: her phone buzzing with the group chat, and this time she types back, 'Everything is fine. Actually, finally, it is.' Emotional beat: earned peace.
